title: Arson: causing great bodily injury
summary: Willfully and maliciously setting fire to, burning, causing, aiding, counseling or procuring a burning, causing great bodily injury. Inhabited means currently used for dwelling, whether or not occupied at the time.
penalty: Felony: 5, 7 or 9 years in state prison. For a felony, section 456(a) permits an additional fine up to $50,000 unless a greater amount applies; for pecuniary gain, section 456(b) instead permits twice the anticipated or actual gross gain. These are base fines, not total financial ceilings. Section 451(e) requires a consecutive sentence for the specified convicted prisoners; section 451.1 aggravators require separate allegation and proof. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review. Arson registration under section 457.1 generally applies for life to adult California convictions on or after November 30, 1994, subject to statutory relief; it is distinct from sex-offender registration. Section 454 can replace these ordinary ranges during and within a Governor-proclaimed emergency or insurrection; that special sentencing branch needs separate review.

title: Aggravated arson
summary: Willful, malicious, deliberate and premeditated burning with the additional injury or property-damage intent stated in section 451.5(a), plus at least one specified aggravator: an arson conviction within 10 years, losses exceeding $10,100,000 excluding damage to inhabited dwellings but including fire suppression, or damage to five or more inhabited dwellings. This is the version operative before January 1, 2029; dollar-threshold amendments apply prospectively.

title: Unlawfully causing a fire: causing great bodily injury
summary: Recklessly setting fire to, burning or causing a burning, causing great bodily injury. Recklessness means consciously disregarding the substantial, unjustifiable fire risk, including unawareness solely from voluntary intoxication; mere accident is insufficient. Inhabited means used for dwelling whether occupied or not.
penalty: Felony or misdemeanor: 2, 4 or 6 years in state prison, or up to one year in county jail, or a fine, or both. For a felony, section 456(a) permits an additional fine up to $50,000 unless a greater amount applies; for pecuniary gain, section 456(b) instead permits twice the anticipated or actual gross gain. These are base fines, not total financial ceilings. The misdemeanor fine ceiling requires separate review and is not stated here. Section 452(e) requires consecutive sentencing for specified convicted prisoners; facilitating organized retail theft within a merchant's premises is a sentencing aggravator under (f). Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review. Section 454 can replace these ordinary ranges during and within a Governor-proclaimed emergency or insurrection; that special sentencing branch needs separate review.

title: Possessing, making or transferring incendiary material with intent to burn
summary: Possessing, manufacturing or disposing of flammable or combustible material or an incendiary device in an arrangement or preparation intended for willful and malicious burning. Authorized official use, scientific or educational use, permitted brush disposal and other lawful burning remain excluded under (c). Ordinary commercially manufactured illumination devices are excluded from the incendiary-device definition.
penalty: Felony or misdemeanor: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h), or up to one year in county jail. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily county jail, subject to state-prison exclusions. For a felony, section 456(a) permits an additional fine up to $50,000 unless a greater amount applies; for pecuniary gain, section 456(b) instead permits twice the anticipated or actual gross gain. These are base fines, not total financial ceilings. Misdemeanor fine exposure requires separate review. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review. Arson registration under section 457.1 generally applies for life to adult California convictions on or after November 30, 1994, subject to statutory relief; it is distinct from sex-offender registration.

title: First degree robbery in concert in an inhabited dwelling
summary: Robbery committed voluntarily in concert with at least two other people within one of the inhabited residences listed in section 213(a)(1)(A). Ordinary robbery or simply having one accomplice does not establish this aggravated branch.
penalty: Felony: 3, 6 or 9 years in state prison. A discretionary base fine up to $10,000 may apply under section 672. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review.

title: Forcibly entering a vehicle with intent to commit theft or a felony
summary: Forcibly entering a vehicle with intent to commit theft or a felony inside. Forcible entry includes specified lock-manipulation tools or electronic devices, or force damaging the exterior. Section 465(d) prohibits conviction under both this section and section 459.
penalty: Felony or misdemeanor: up to one year in county jail, or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h), ordinarily county jail subject to state-prison exclusions. A discretionary section 672 base fine may be up to $1,000 for a misdemeanor or $10,000 for a felony. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review.

title: Possessing burglary tools or making unauthorized keys or instruments
summary: Possessing specified tools with intent to feloniously break or enter; knowingly making or altering a key or instrument to open a listed lock without a request from someone entitled to open it; or making, altering or repairing an instrument knowing or having reason to believe it will be used in a misdemeanor or felony. Mere lawful possession of a screwdriver or key device is not enough.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to six months in county jail, a base fine up to $1,000, or both under section 19. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review.

title: Extorting property or consideration by force or threat
summary: Obtaining property or other consideration by wrongful force or a section 519 threat, under circumstances not amounting to robbery or carjacking. Threats include exposing a secret, accusing a person or family member of crime, or reporting actual or suspected immigration status. Section 518(c) excludes a person under 18 who obtains the specified sexual or intimate-image consideration.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3 or 4 years under section 1170(h), ordinarily in county jail subject to state-prison exclusions. A discretionary base fine up to $10,000 may apply under section 672. Adult base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
